title: Lincoln - Lack of Upstream HO2S Switching Bank 1
shortDescription: The upstream heated O2 sensor in bank 1 is not switching between rich and lean as expected.
fullDescription:
This Lincoln-specific code sets when the powertrain control module detects that the upstream heated oxygen sensor on bank 1 is staying near a fixed voltage instead of switching cleanly between rich and lean states. The PCM relies on this switching to trim fuel and maintain stoichiometric operation.

Common causes include a degraded oxygen sensor, a vacuum leak biasing the air-fuel ratio, contamination from coolant or silicone, or wiring issues affecting the heater circuit.

Left unrepaired, the code reduces fuel economy, increases emissions, and may eventually trigger catalyst efficiency codes.
safetyImpact: No immediate safety concern but reduced fuel economy and increased emissions; long-term operation can damage the catalytic converter.

fixSteps.title: Scan and confirm
fixSteps.instruction: Connect scan tool, confirm P1130 and view live O2 sensor 1/1 voltage. Voltage should oscillate 0.1-0.9V at idle when warm.

fixSteps.title: Check vacuum leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect intake gaskets, PCV hoses, and brake booster hose with a smoke tester.

fixSteps.title: Replace upstream O2
fixSteps.instruction: Remove bank 1 upstream sensor with O2 socket and install new sensor with anti-seize.

faq.a: Short term yes, but fuel economy drops and prolonged operation can damage the catalytic converter.
Bank 1 contains cylinder #1; consult the underhood emissions decal for orientation.

title: Lincoln - HO2S-11 Indicates Lean
shortDescription: Upstream HO2S on bank 1 indicates a continuously lean condition.
fullDescription:
This code sets when the bank 1 upstream HO2S reports a lean exhaust stream that fuel trims cannot correct within calibration limits. The PCM has added maximum positive long-term fuel trim without bringing the sensor back to switching range.

Lincoln vehicles with this code typically suffer from unmetered air entering after the MAF, low fuel pressure, or dirty injectors. A coked intake on direct-injection 3.5L EcoBoost or 3.7L Duratec can also bias readings lean at idle.

If ignored, the engine may run rough at idle and the catalyst can overheat from prolonged lean operation.
safetyImpact: Lean operation increases combustion temperatures and can damage pistons and the catalyst over time.

fixSteps.title: Read fuel trims
fixSteps.instruction: Check STFT and LTFT on bank 1; values above +20% confirm lean.

fixSteps.title: Test fuel pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Connect fuel pressure gauge at the rail and verify Lincoln spec at idle and load.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test intake
fixSteps.instruction: Smoke test from throttle body to PCV system to find unmetered air leaks.

faq.a: Yes — clean with sensor-safe cleaner before condemning components.
Quality cleaner over several tanks can help mild fouling.

title: Lincoln - EGR Flow Out of Self-Test Range
shortDescription: EGR system flow rate during self-test is outside expected range on a Lincoln.
fullDescription:
Lincoln models such as Town Car, Continental, and older LS use a Differential Pressure Feedback EGR (DPFE) system. P1408 sets when the PCM commands EGR flow during self-test and the DPFE response is too high or too low.

Most commonly the cause is a clogged EGR passage, a failed DPFE sensor, or cracked DPFE hoses. A stuck EGR valve or vacuum control solenoid will also fail the test.

This code typically appears alongside P0401, P0402, or P1406 and may cause hesitation, rough idle, or detonation under load.
safetyImpact: Improper EGR flow can lead to detonation and accelerated engine wear.

fixSteps.title: Inspect DPFE hoses
fixSteps.instruction: Remove DPFE and check the two silicone hoses for cracks or carbon clogs.

fixSteps.title: Clean EGR passages
fixSteps.instruction: Remove EGR valve and clean carbon from valve and intake passages.

fixSteps.title: Test DPFE sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Compare DPFE voltage at rest and under vacuum to spec.

No — bypassing fails inspection and causes detonation.

title: Lincoln - EGR Vacuum Regulator Solenoid Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault detected in the EGR vacuum regulator solenoid circuit.
fullDescription:
The EGR vacuum regulator (EVR) solenoid receives a duty-cycled signal from the PCM. P1409 sets when the PCM detects an open, short to ground, or short to power in the EVR control circuit.

Causes range from a failed solenoid coil, chafed wiring near the engine cover or exhaust manifold, to a corroded connector. Less commonly the PCM driver itself has failed.

With this code present the EGR system is disabled and the engine may detonate under load.
safetyImpact: Disabled EGR can cause detonation, NOx spikes, and emissions inspection failure.

fixSteps.title: Check EVR resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect EVR connector and measure coil resistance against Lincoln spec (26-37 ohms).

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Wiggle test harness from EVR to PCM looking for breaks.

fixSteps.title: Replace EVR solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Mount new EVR and reconnect lines and connector.

faq.a: It will return — repair the circuit fault.
Yes — heat near exhaust degrades insulation.

title: GMC - CKP-CMP Correlation
shortDescription: Crankshaft and camshaft position sensor signals do not correlate within GM specification.
fullDescription:
On GMC trucks and SUVs equipped with Vortec V8 (5.3L, 6.0L) and 4.8L engines, P1345 sets when the PCM compares CKP and CMP signals and finds a mismatch greater than the calibrated threshold for one or more revolutions.

The most common cause on GMT800 and GMT900 trucks is a stretched or jumped timing chain. Failed CMP/CKP sensors and a damaged reluctor wheel can also produce this code.

Ignoring the code can lead to valve-to-piston contact if the chain skips additional teeth.
safetyImpact: A jumped timing chain can result in catastrophic engine damage. Address promptly.

fixSteps.title: Capture freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: Document RPM, load, and cam phasing. Note related DTCs (P0008, P0017).

fixSteps.title: Check timing chain stretch
fixSteps.instruction: Command cam advance with bidirectional tool and observe response.

fixSteps.title: Replace timing chain assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Replace chain, guides, tensioner, and sprockets.

faq.a: Yes — early AFM-equipped Vortec engines are documented for chain stretch.
Sometimes; if chain is good and sensor reads erratically, CMP fixes it.

title: GMC - Ignition Control Circuit High Voltage
shortDescription: PCM has detected high voltage on the ignition control circuit on a GMC vehicle.
fullDescription:
P1351 sets when the PCM monitors the ignition control reference voltage and finds it higher than expected. This typically points to a problem in the ICM or a coil driver circuit on older GMC distributor-based engines.

On newer coil-on-plug GMC engines this code can indicate a wiring issue between PCM and coil pack, or a failed ignition module.

The engine may have a no-start, intermittent stall, or single-cylinder misfire when active.
safetyImpact: Misfires can damage the catalytic converter; no-start strands the vehicle.

fixSteps.title: Verify spark
fixSteps.instruction: Use spark tester at each plug or coil to find the dead cylinder.

fixSteps.title: Backprobe IC circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe ignition control wire and watch for square wave during crank.

fixSteps.title: Replace ICM or coil
fixSteps.instruction: Replace failed module or coil and recheck.

faq.q: Will it run on the others?
faq.a: Yes but heavy misfire and possible stall.
Recommended at high mileage.

title: GMC - Secondary AIR Injection System Bank 1
shortDescription: Secondary air injection on bank 1 is not delivering expected airflow.
fullDescription:
GMC trucks and SUVs (4.8L, 5.3L, 6.0L) use an electric pump to push fresh air into the exhaust at cold start to accelerate catalyst light-off. P1415 sets when the PCM commands the system on and bank 1 O2 does not see the expected lean shift.

Failed pumps, stuck check valves, broken pipes, and rusted air rails are common on northern-state trucks. Water ingestion damages pump motor brushes.

The vehicle passes through a cold start without proper catalyst preheat.
safetyImpact: No drivability impact in most cases, but emissions inspection will fail.

fixSteps.title: Activate pump test
fixSteps.instruction: Use bidirectional control to run AIR pump.

fixSteps.title: Inspect check valves
fixSteps.instruction: Remove valves and confirm they pass air one direction only.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace pump, valve, or rusted pipe.

faq.a: No — emissions equipment monitored by OBD-II.
Water vapor freezes and breaks the pump impeller.

title: GMC - Secondary AIR Injection System Bank 2
shortDescription: Secondary air injection on bank 2 is not delivering expected airflow.
fullDescription:
Identical fault logic to P1415 but for the bank 2 (passenger side on most V8) air injection rail. The PCM monitors the bank 2 upstream O2 during the cold-start AIR test and flags this code if the lean shift is missing.

A single failed pump can set both P1415 and P1416. A bank-specific check valve failure typically sets only one code.

Cold-start emissions increase but drivability is generally unaffected.
safetyImpact: Emissions inspection failure but no drivability or safety concern.

fixSteps.title: Run pump test
fixSteps.instruction: Activate pump with scan tool and verify airflow at each port.

fixSteps.title: Replace bank 2 check valve
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and replace bank 2 check valve at the manifold port.

fixSteps.title: Inspect tubing
fixSteps.instruction: Look for rust-through or split sections from pump to check valve.

faq.a: Yes — corroded steel air lines are common on northern trucks.
Passenger side on GM small-block V8.

title: Isuzu - Fuel Rail Pressure Low During Cranking
shortDescription: Fuel rail pressure is below threshold during cranking on Isuzu diesel.
fullDescription:
Isuzu 4HK1 and 6HK1 common-rail diesels report P1094 when the fuel pressure sensor reads below the calibrated minimum during cranking. The ECM cannot inject fuel safely below this threshold and will extend cranking or refuse to start.

Causes include a failing supply pump (HP3/HP4), suction control valve issue, air entering through a loose fuel line, or a clogged filter. Worn injector return flow can also keep rail pressure from building.

Vehicles exhibit long crank, no-start, or stall after cold soak.
safetyImpact: No-start can strand a commercial vehicle; injector damage from prolonged cranking is possible.

fixSteps.title: Bleed and replace filter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace fuel filter, drain water separator, prime per Isuzu procedure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect SCV
fixSteps.instruction: Remove SCV and inspect for debris.

fixSteps.title: Pressure-test pump
fixSteps.instruction: Use Isuzu IDSS to command rail pressure and verify pump output.

faq.a: Only if fuel quality is the cause.
Yes — SCV failures are documented on the 4HK1.

title: Isuzu - A/F Sensor Bank 1 Sensor 1 Low Voltage
shortDescription: Air-fuel ratio sensor on bank 1 is reading below specification.
fullDescription:
Isuzu Trooper, Rodeo, and Ascender models with wideband A/F sensors set P1273 when the sensor reports voltage below the lean-rich threshold for an extended period. The ECM cannot fuel correctly without valid A/F input.

Common causes include a failed sensor element, contamination from silicone or coolant, an open heater circuit, or a wiring fault. Exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor can also bias readings.

Driveability impact ranges from mild rich/lean correction loss to noticeable rough running.
safetyImpact: Increased fuel consumption and emissions; potential catalyst damage if rich.

fixSteps.title: Read sensor data
fixSteps.instruction: Verify lambda and heater current with scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for exhaust leak
fixSteps.instruction: Check manifold and pipe ahead of A/F sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace A/F sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace bank 1 sensor 1 with OEM Denso.

faq.a: Wideband reports exact AFR over a wide range.
OEM Denso is recommended.

title: Isuzu - EGR Closed Position Performance
shortDescription: EGR valve does not return fully to the closed position.
fullDescription:
On Isuzu gas and diesel models with electric EGR, P1404 sets when the EGR position sensor indicates the valve is not seating fully closed when commanded. Carbon buildup on the valve seat is the most common cause.

A stuck-open EGR creates rough idle, hesitation off idle, and increased emissions. Severe carbon can also damage the EGR position sensor.

Resolution typically involves removing and cleaning the valve, but heavily fouled valves should be replaced.
safetyImpact: Rough idle and hesitation; possible failed emissions inspection.

fixSteps.title: Remove and inspect EGR
fixSteps.instruction: Unbolt EGR valve and inspect seat and pintle.

fixSteps.title: Clean valve and ports
fixSteps.instruction: Carefully clean with throttle body cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Replace if scored
fixSteps.instruction: Replace EGR if seat or pintle pitted.

faq.a: No — monitored by OBD-II.
Every 60-100k on older diesels.

title: Scion - Igniter Circuit Malfunction No.1
shortDescription: Ignition igniter (coil) circuit fault on cylinder 1.
fullDescription:
Scion xA, xB, tC, iQ, and FR-S use coil-on-plug ignition with internal igniters. P1300 sets when the ECM does not see expected ignition confirmation from cylinder 1's coil during firing.

Failed coil packs are the leading cause, particularly with age and heat soak. Wiring issues, ECM driver failure, and bad ground are secondary causes.

The engine will misfire on the affected cylinder and may set additional misfire codes.
safetyImpact: Misfire can damage catalytic converter if sustained.

fixSteps.title: Swap coils to confirm
fixSteps.instruction: Move cyl 1 coil elsewhere — fault should follow.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM-quality coil pack.

fixSteps.title: Replace plug if old
fixSteps.instruction: Install fresh iridium plug at high mileage.

faq.a: Stick with Denso/NGK OEM-equivalent.
Reasonable preventive maintenance at high mileage.

title: Scion - VVT System Malfunction Bank 1
shortDescription: Variable valve timing system on bank 1 is not responding to ECM commands.
fullDescription:
Scion vehicles with VVT-i or dual VVT-i set P1349 when commanded cam advance does not match actual cam position. Low or contaminated oil starves the OCV and VVT actuator.

A failed oil control valve (OCV) is the most common cause. Sludge clogging the OCV screen is widespread on neglected engines. Severe cases involve a worn cam phaser.

The engine may rough idle, lose power, and show poor fuel economy.
safetyImpact: Loss of valve timing control reduces power and efficiency; can lead to chain wear.

fixSteps.title: Verify oil
fixSteps.instruction: Check oil level and condition; change with correct spec.

fixSteps.title: Clean OCV
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the bank 1 OCV, clean screen, replace if not clicking.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cam phaser
fixSteps.instruction: If OCV good, inspect phaser for wear.

faq.a: Yes — clogged OCV screens are common.
Use only spec viscosity.

title: Scion - Knock Control CPU
shortDescription: Internal ECM knock control processor failure.
fullDescription:
P1605 indicates that the ECM has detected an internal fault in its knock control logic. The ECM uses the knock sensor input to retard timing under load; if this circuitry fails the engine may run very conservatively or produce knock under throttle.

This code is typically caused by an internal ECM fault and is rarely repairable outside of ECM replacement or reprogramming. Verify the knock sensor circuit before condemning the ECM.

Vehicles may exhibit reduced power, poor mileage, and rough running under load.
safetyImpact: Loss of knock control can permit detonation under high load and damage pistons.

fixSteps.title: Test knock sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance and check for shorts.

fixSteps.title: Reprogram or replace ECM
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer reflash or replacement required.

fixSteps.title: Verify with Techstream
fixSteps.instruction: Toyota Techstream confirms internal fault flag.

faq.a: Often — but rule out wiring first.
Reduces knock but does not fix underlying fault.

title: Lexus - A/F Sensor Heater Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
shortDescription: Air-fuel sensor heater circuit on bank 1 sensor 1 is not operating within spec.
fullDescription:
Lexus vehicles with wideband A/F sensors monitor heater current to ensure quick warm-up. P1135 sets when heater current is out of range, indicating an open, short, or sensor failure.

The wideband A/F sensor is more expensive than a traditional O2 and shares failure modes with age and heat. Wiring damage near the exhaust and corroded connectors are also causes.

The vehicle runs in open loop until the sensor heats — fuel economy and emissions suffer.
safetyImpact: Open-loop fueling reduces fuel economy and increases emissions.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse and relay
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect EFI/AFS fuse and relay.

fixSteps.title: Measure heater resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect sensor and check coil resistance.

fixSteps.title: Replace A/F sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace with Denso OEM unit only.

faq.a: No — Lexus widebands are not interchangeable with narrowband O2.
Typically 100k+ miles unless oil-contaminated.

title: Lexus - VVT System Malfunction
shortDescription: Variable valve timing actuator response is out of specification.
fullDescription:
Most Lexus models with VVT-i (IS, GS, ES, RX) use an oil control valve and cam phaser. P1349 sets when actual cam position lags or leads commanded position outside acceptable error.

Low or contaminated oil is the leading cause. The OCV solenoid screen can clog with sludge, blocking pressure to the cam phaser. In late-stage failure the cam phaser locking pin wears and the actuator chatters at idle.

Driveability suffers with rough idle, hesitation, and a noticeable rattle on cold start.
safetyImpact: Long-term operation with VVT errors increases timing chain wear and oil consumption.

fixSteps.title: Change oil
fixSteps.instruction: Use exact viscosity called for; address sludge with quality oil.

fixSteps.title: Service OCV
fixSteps.instruction: Remove OCV and clean or replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace cam phaser
fixSteps.instruction: If rattle persists, replace cam phaser.

faq.a: Missed oil changes plug the small OCV screen.
Avoid solvent flushes — frequent fresh oil is safer.

title: Lexus - Knock Sensor Control Module
shortDescription: Knock control circuit inside ECM has reported a fault.
fullDescription:
Lexus models with knock-sensor-driven ignition timing report P1605 when the internal knock-control monitor detects an out-of-range value. The ECM may use a default conservative timing map until cleared.

Common root causes include the knock sensor itself, harness damage where it routes near the exhaust, or in some cases an internal ECM fault. Some IS300 and GS300 models have known harness chafe points to inspect first.

Underhood power feels reduced and fuel economy may drop.
safetyImpact: Loss of knock control increases risk of detonation under load.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect knock sensor sub-harness under intake plenum.

fixSteps.title: Test knock sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance and check for shorts.

fixSteps.title: Replace ECM if needed
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer repair/replace if wiring and sensor good.

faq.a: Yes briefly; use premium and avoid heavy throttle.
Sits under intake — labor heavy.

title: Acura - MAP Higher Than Expected
shortDescription: MAP sensor reading is higher than expected for current engine operating conditions.
fullDescription:
Acura models including TL, TSX, MDX, and RDX use MAP and MAF together. P1129 sets when MAP reads higher than the calibrated model expects, suggesting a vacuum issue, sensor bias, or stuck-open EGR.

A stuck EGR or restricted intake VTEC solenoid can also disturb MAP readings. Aftermarket intakes that disturb the MAP signal hose are known causes on TSX models.

Driveability ranges from mild hesitation to a check-engine light only.
safetyImpact: Mild driveability impact and slightly higher emissions.

fixSteps.title: Inspect vacuum hose
fixSteps.instruction: Check MAP signal hose for kinks or oil.

fixSteps.title: Test MAP sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Compare MAP at idle to barometric pressure with key on engine off.

fixSteps.title: Service EGR
fixSteps.instruction: Clean or replace EGR if stuck.

faq.a: Usually mild — but stuck EGR can cause stalls.
Aggressive tunes can; revert to stock and retest.

title: Acura - Electrical Load Detector Circuit High
shortDescription: Electrical load detector signal voltage is above expected range.
fullDescription:
Acura's ELD monitors total electrical load to allow the PCM to manage alternator output. P1297 sets when ELD voltage reads higher than spec, often due to a failed ELD unit in the underhood fuse box.

The alternator may overcharge or undercharge until repaired, shortening battery life. Wiring issues to the ELD plug can cause similar symptoms.

The code is generally cleared by replacing the plug-in ELD unit.
safetyImpact: Possible undercharging or overcharging the battery.

causes.cause: Open wire from ELD to PCM

fixSteps.title: Inspect ELD socket
fixSteps.instruction: Open underhood fuse box and inspect socket.

fixSteps.title: Replace ELD
fixSteps.instruction: Pull failed ELD and install new OEM unit.

fixSteps.title: Verify charging
fixSteps.instruction: Test charging at idle and 2000 RPM.

faq.a: No — PCM relies on signal.
Verify output after replacing ELD.

title: Acura - EVAP Leak Detected (Fuel Tank)
shortDescription: EVAP system has detected a leak originating from the fuel tank side.
fullDescription:
Acura uses a fuel tank pressure sensor and bypass solenoid for evap leak detection. P1456 specifically flags a leak on the fuel tank side rather than the canister side.

A loose or failed fuel cap is the most common cause, followed by the fuel filler neck recall (older TL/MDX), a damaged tank seal, or a failed fuel tank pressure sensor. Newer models may also flag this for ORVR check valve issues.

The vehicle runs normally but will fail emissions and emit hydrocarbons.
safetyImpact: Hydrocarbon emissions; inspection failure but no drivability issue.

fixSteps.title: Tighten/replace cap
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten until it clicks; replace if cracked.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test tank side
fixSteps.instruction: Use EVAP smoke tester.

fixSteps.title: Inspect filler neck
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect for rust on northern Acuras.

faq.a: Often yes; clear and run drive cycle.
Some Acura models had recalls — check VIN.

title: Genesis - Knock Sensor Detection System (KSDS)
shortDescription: KSDS algorithm has identified abnormal vibration patterns suggesting connecting rod bearing wear.
fullDescription:
Genesis models powered by the Theta II 2.0T or Lambda V6 may set P1326 when the KSDS algorithm detects characteristic vibrations associated with bearing damage. This is the same algorithm rolled out across Hyundai/Kia/Genesis as part of the bearing-failure recall.

When P1326 sets, the ECM enters Engine Protection Mode that limits RPM. Continuing to drive risks complete engine seizure.

Genesis vehicles within recall coverage may qualify for a free engine inspection or replacement.
safetyImpact: Engine seizure risk if driven hard. Limp mode limits highway driving safely.

fixSteps.title: Verify with dealer scan
fixSteps.instruction: Genesis dealer can read KSDS event data.

fixSteps.title: Engine replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Short or long block replacement if confirmed.

fixSteps.title: Check recall
fixSteps.instruction: Verify VIN against open recalls.

Many Theta II covered — check VIN.

title: Genesis - Unable to Bleed Fuel Tank Vacuum
shortDescription: Vehicle cannot relieve EVAP-induced fuel tank vacuum within calibrated time.
fullDescription:
Genesis uses a sealed EVAP system with a fuel tank isolation valve. P1450 sets when the system applies vacuum during a leak test and cannot bleed it back to atmospheric within the expected window.

A stuck closed canister vent valve (CVV) is the leading cause. A blocked vent line or saturated charcoal canister can also cause this code. After refueling without removing the cap correctly, the symptom may recur.

The vehicle drives normally but will fail emissions monitor readiness.
safetyImpact: No drivability or safety impact; emissions readiness failure.

fixSteps.title: Activate CVV
fixSteps.instruction: Bidirectional control to cycle vent valve.

fixSteps.title: Inspect vent hose
fixSteps.instruction: Trace from canister to atmosphere.

fixSteps.title: Replace CVV
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and replace canister vent valve.

Before next emissions inspection.

title: Genesis - Battery Sensor Communication Error
shortDescription: IBS battery management sensor has stopped reporting to the ECM.
fullDescription:
Genesis vehicles use an Intelligent Battery Sensor (IBS) on the negative battery terminal to monitor state of charge, current, and temperature. P1550 sets when LIN communication between IBS and ECM is lost or returns invalid data.

Direct causes include loose terminal, corroded ring, damaged IBS pigtail, or failed IBS module. After installing a new battery without registration the IBS may also flag inconsistencies.

Symptoms include reduced charging, ECO/start-stop disabled, and battery warnings.
safetyImpact: Reduced charging strategy can shorten battery life; start-stop disabled.

fixSteps.title: Tighten terminal
fixSteps.instruction: Re-terminate the negative cable.

fixSteps.title: Register battery
fixSteps.instruction: Run dealer-tool battery registration after replacement.

fixSteps.title: Replace IBS
fixSteps.instruction: Replace IBS sensor on negative cable.

Yes — Genesis requires it after battery replacement.

title: Genesis - Tail Lamp Relay Drive Circuit
shortDescription: Fault detected in tail lamp relay drive circuit.
fullDescription:
Some Genesis models monitor body relays through BCM and ECM combined. P1693 sets when the BCM cannot drive the tail lamp relay or sees unexpected feedback voltage.

Most cases involve a failed relay, blown fuse, or chafed wire to the rear. Aftermarket trailer wiring can also short the circuit and trigger the code.

Functionally, tail lamps may flicker or stay off — a safety concern.
safetyImpact: Tail lamps may not function — significant rear-visibility risk at night.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse and relay
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect tail lamp fuse and relay.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect trailer wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Recheck after disconnecting aftermarket harness.

fixSteps.title: Inspect rear harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check trunk hinges and rear bumper.

faq.a: Not at night.
Often yes — try a known-good relay.

title: Smart - MAF Sensor Range/Performance
shortDescription: MAF sensor signal on a Smart Fortwo is out of expected range.
fullDescription:
Smart Fortwo (450/451) uses a small Bosch MAF. P1100 sets when MAF readings disagree with throttle position and RPM by more than calibration allows.

Dirty sensor element, vacuum leak, intake boot tear, or clogged air filter are common. The 0.8L CDI diesel and 1.0L gas both share similar logic.

Symptoms include hesitation, surge at cruise, and loss of pep.
safetyImpact: Reduced engine performance; slight emissions increase.

fixSteps.instruction: Open rear engine bay and flex boot for splits.

title: Smart - Misfire Cylinder 1
shortDescription: Misfire detected on cylinder 1 of a Smart Fortwo.
fullDescription:
Smart's three-cylinder gas and diesel engines (M132 and OM660) can misfire from worn coils, fouled plugs, or low compression. P1300 specifically flags cylinder 1.

Low oil and skipped service intervals make plug fouling more likely. Coil packs are individually replaceable; shared ignition wiring on early 450 models can cross-fire when wires age.

Sustained misfire can damage the catalyst.
safetyImpact: Catalyst damage from sustained misfire.

fixSteps.instruction: If misfire persists, test compression.

Yes — heat soak shortens life.

title: Smart - Starter Motor Signal
shortDescription: Starter motor signal circuit fault on Smart Fortwo.
fullDescription:
Smart vehicles monitor the starter signal between EIS/ignition and starter solenoid. P1500 sets when the ECM does not see crank engagement during a start attempt or sees the signal at unexpected times.

Failed starter solenoids, corroded battery terminals, and EIS module issues are common. Many 451 owners report this code after weak-battery starts.

Intermittent no-start is the typical symptom.

Maybach 57 and 62, sharing platform with Mercedes S-Class W220, use a sequential injection system on V12 biturbo or V8 powertrains. P1200 sets when the ME detects an open in one of the injector control circuits.

Failed injector solenoid, corroded connector, or harness chafe are common. The V12 layout makes coil/injector access deep beneath the intake plenum.

Misfire on the affected cylinder is the typical impact.

shortDescription: Ignition coil primary circuit fault on a Maybach engine.
fullDescription:
Maybach 57/62 V12 BiTurbo (M275) uses individual coil-on-plug units. P1300 sets on a primary circuit fault — open, short, or driver failure on a specific cylinder.

These coils sit under the engine cover and are heat-soaked in the V-valley. Bosch coils have finite life and benefit from sets-of-12 replacement at 100k miles. Boot tracking and carbon path failures are also common.

Maybach diesel powertrains and some gas variants with EGR use a position sensor on the EGR valve. P1400 sets when the position signal does not match commanded position or remains out of range.

Carbon buildup on the valve and worn sensor potentiometer are leading causes. After cleaning, position adaptation must be reset using XENTRY.

Loss of EGR control increases NOx and may cause hesitation off idle.

title: Bentley - Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
shortDescription: Cylinder 1 misfire on a Bentley vehicle.
fullDescription:
Bentley Continental, Flying Spur, and Bentayga use W12 or V8 powertrains shared with VW Group. P1300 indicates a misfire on cylinder 1 confirmed by crank speed analysis.

Ignition coil failure is the most common cause. Coil packs in the W12 sit deep in tight valleys. Carbon buildup on intake valves of TFSI/TSI engines can also cause misfire.

Flashing CEL signals catalyst risk.

fixSteps.instruction: Walnut shell intake valve cleaning if carbon.

Yes when done by trained tech.

title: Bentley - TCM Performance
shortDescription: Transmission control module performance fault on a Bentley vehicle.
fullDescription:
Bentley uses ZF 8HP and earlier 6-speed automatics. P1700 indicates the TCM is reporting performance outside expected operating envelope, often due to mechatronic issues, fluid temperature out of range, or solenoid wear.

Fluid never being changed is a primary contributor on older units; ZF spec recommends service at 60-80k miles. A failing mechatronic seal can let fluid migrate into the TCM.

Harsh shifts or limp mode may result.
safetyImpact: Limp mode and harsh shifting affect drivability and safety.

Sometimes; persistent needs diagnosis.

title: Bentley - Air Suspension Compressor Performance
shortDescription: Air suspension compressor is not maintaining required pressure.
fullDescription:
Bentley Continental and Bentayga use air suspension. P1800 sets when the compressor runs but pressure does not reach setpoint within calibrated time. Leaks in struts, lines, or valve block are common.

The compressor itself may also be worn and unable to build pressure. On cold mornings the system may take longer than acceptable to lift the vehicle.

Driving with low pressure can damage the compressor.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may sag at one corner; handling unpredictable.

fixSteps.instruction: Replace compressor or strut.

title: Rolls-Royce - Misfire Detected Cylinder 1

fullDescription:
Rolls-Royce Phantom, Ghost, Wraith, and Cullinan use BMW-derived V12 (N73/N74) powertrains. P1300 confirms misfire on cylinder 1 via crankshaft speed monitoring.

Ignition coil failure is the leading cause due to thermal cycling. Spark plug life is around 60k miles; long-life iridium plugs are spec. Vanos solenoid issues can also cause cylinder-specific misfires.

The vehicle will reduce power to protect the catalyst.
safetyImpact: Catalyst damage and engine power reduction.

fixSteps.instruction: BMW ISTA confirms cylinder.

Cramped V12 valley plus dealer-only parts.

title: Rolls-Royce - Starter Motor Circuit
shortDescription: Starter motor control circuit fault on a Rolls-Royce vehicle.
fullDescription:
Rolls-Royce vehicles with start-stop systems run the starter under high duty cycle. P1500 sets when the DME does not see expected starter response or current draw.

Weak battery, corroded cables, or a failing starter contactor cause this code. Some Phantom owners report relay failure in the underhood power distribution box.

No-start or extended crank is typical.
safetyImpact: Intermittent no-start can strand the vehicle.

Use designated jump terminals only.

title: Aston Martin - Transmission Indeterminate Failure
shortDescription: Transmission has reported a fault that prevents normal operation.
fullDescription:
Aston Martin DB9, Vantage, and Rapide use ZF 6HP/8HP transaxles or Graziano automated manuals. P1700 indicates the TCU has reported an indeterminate failure preventing shift execution.

Low fluid, mechatronic faults, and clutch wear (on automated manuals) are major causes. The Sportshift on V8 Vantage in particular has known clutch and actuator wear.

Limp mode or no-engagement results.
safetyImpact: Limp mode or no engagement; vehicle may need flatbed.

fixSteps.instruction: Service clutch or mechatronic.

No — specialized procedures required.

title: Aston Martin - Brake Booster Vacuum Performance
shortDescription: Brake booster vacuum performance fault.
fullDescription:
Aston Martin V8 and V12 models use engine vacuum or electric vacuum pump for brake assist. P1800 sets when the booster vacuum sensor reports insufficient vacuum during expected conditions.

Vacuum hose leaks, failed check valve, or worn vacuum pump (on V8) cause this code. The booster diaphragm itself can leak with age and high mileage.

Safety-critical because brake pedal effort increases significantly.
safetyImpact: Increased brake effort — direct safety concern. Repair immediately.

fixSteps.instruction: Check from manifold/pump to booster.

title: McLaren - Turbo Boost Pressure Lower Than Desired
shortDescription: Boost pressure on a McLaren M838T or M840T engine is lower than commanded.
fullDescription:
McLaren 12C, 650S, 720S, and Artura use twin-turbo V8 or V6 hybrid powertrains. P1600 sets when actual boost lags commanded setpoint by a calibrated margin.

Boost leaks at intercooler couplers, wastegate actuator wear, dirty MAF or charge-air sensor, and turbo bearing wear are causes. Software updates have addressed early-car wastegate calibration issues.

Reduced power and slower acceleration result.
safetyImpact: Reduced performance; long-term operation can stress turbos.

Voids warranty and can damage turbos.

title: McLaren - DCT Line Pressure Low
shortDescription: DCT line pressure below threshold on a McLaren vehicle.
fullDescription:
McLaren's SSG dual-clutch transmission requires precise hydraulic pressure for clutch engagement. P1700 sets when the TCU reads line pressure below threshold during shifts.

Low fluid, clogged filter, worn pressure pump, or failed pressure sensor cause this code. McLaren TCT fluid service intervals are critical and often missed.

Hard shifts, slipping clutches, and limp mode can occur.
safetyImpact: Slipping clutches can fail catastrophically and require costly rebuild.

fixSteps.instruction: Pump, sensor, or rebuild.

Every 3 years or 25,000 miles.

title: Ferrari - EGR Valve Position Sensor
shortDescription: EGR valve position fault on a Ferrari turbocharged model.
fullDescription:
Ferrari turbo models like the 488 and Roma use EGR for emissions compliance in some markets. P1400 sets when the EGR position sensor disagrees with commanded position.

Carbon buildup is the major cause; track use can offset this with high-temperature operation but daily driving accelerates buildup.

Mild drivability impact and emissions inspection failure.
safetyImpact: Emissions failure and slight power loss.

Helps but doesn't eliminate.

title: Ferrari - ECU Internal Communication Error
shortDescription: Internal ECU communication fault on a Ferrari vehicle.
fullDescription:
Modern Ferraris use multiple control units networked over CAN with the master engine ECU. P1600 sets when the ECU detects internal communication faults — often with a fuel pump driver, ignition driver module, or coprocessor.

Causes include software corruption (resolvable via reflash), failed ECU drivers, or a chassis ground issue.

Drivability ranges from rough running to no-start.
safetyImpact: Possible no-start; serious if fault prevents safe operation.

title: Ferrari - F1/DCT Hydraulic Pressure Low
shortDescription: F1 paddle-shift or DCT transmission hydraulic pressure below threshold.
fullDescription:
Ferrari F430, 599, and 458 use either F1 (automated manual) or DCT transmissions. P1700 indicates that hydraulic pressure for clutch and shift actuation is below threshold.

Fluid leaks at the actuator, worn pump, or failed pressure sensor cause this. F1 actuators are known to wear with age, requiring rebuild.

Hard shifts, no shift, or limp mode result.
safetyImpact: No drive or limp mode; can require flatbed.

DCT smoother; F1 more mechanical.

shortDescription: Mass air flow sensor signal out of range.
fullDescription:
Lamborghini Gallardo, Huracan, and Aventador use Audi/VW-derived MAF sensors. P1100 sets when MAF readings are inconsistent with throttle position and RPM under closed-loop fueling.

Dirty MAF, intake pipe leak, or failed MAF sensor are common. The cramped engine bay can heat-age the MAF.

Reduced power and check engine light result.
safetyImpact: Reduced performance and emissions impact.

Every 30k as preventive.

shortDescription: Cylinder 1 fuel injector circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Lamborghini's V10 and V12 powertrains use sequential injection. P1200 indicates an open or shorted control circuit on cylinder 1's injector.

Failed injector solenoid, harness chafing, or corroded connector are likely. Aftermarket exhaust headers can route heat near injector wiring on Gallardo.

Misfire on cylinder 1 results.

shortDescription: Cylinder 1 misfire on a Lamborghini engine.
fullDescription:
P1300 confirms misfire on cylinder 1 via crank speed analysis. On Lamborghini V10/V12 engines, ignition coil failures and worn plugs are leading causes. Carbon on direct injection valves can also cause misfire on FSI/TFSI variants.

Flashing CEL during misfire indicates immediate catalyst risk.
safetyImpact: Catalyst damage if sustained.

shortDescription: Bank 1 cam timing actual position diverges from commanded.
fullDescription:
Lamborghini V10 and V12 engines use variable cam timing for power and emissions. P1400 sets when cam advance does not respond within tolerance.

Low oil pressure, failed cam phaser solenoid, or chain wear are likely causes. Track use with high RPM accelerates chain wear.

Reduced power and rough idle result.
safetyImpact: Long-term operation can damage timing chain and phaser.

title: Maserati - Fuel Pump Relay Circuit
shortDescription: Fuel pump relay control circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Maserati QuattroPorte, Ghibli, and Levante use a fuel pump relay controlled by the ECU. P1500 sets when the ECU does not see expected feedback voltage on the relay control circuit.

Failed relay, blown fuse, or wiring to the pump relay are likely. Long-crank or no-start can occur.

Vehicle drivability is significantly affected.
safetyImpact: No-start can strand the vehicle.

fullDescription:
P1600 indicates the ECU has detected an internal hardware or software fault. Cause may be a power supply issue, software corruption, or driver failure.

Reflashing at the dealer often resolves software-induced faults. Hardware faults require ECU replacement and re-coding to chassis VIN.

Drivability ranges from limp mode to no-start.
safetyImpact: Possible no-start or limp mode.

Reduced power and surge result.

The sensor may be aged, contaminated by oil or coolant, or its heater circuit may be slow to bring it to operating temperature. Wiring corrosion at the firewall connector is also common in older VE/VF Commodores.

Holden 4L60E and 6L80 transmissions request a momentary torque cut from the ECM during shifts. P1779 indicates the ECM saw an invalid request, or the TCM never confirmed the cut.

Typical causes are CAN bus wiring faults, a failing TCM, or a software calibration mismatch after a module swap.

causes.cause: Wiring chafe at exhaust manifold heat shield

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect EFI/AFR heater fuse in engine bay.

fixSteps.title: Measure heater resistance

fixSteps.title: Replace AFR sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Use Toyota OE sensor for proper calibration.

faq.a: Always use Denso OE for AFR; aftermarket often miscalibrates.

title: Pilot EVAP Canister Leak
shortDescription: Honda Pilot evaporative emissions canister-side leak detected.
fullDescription:
The Pilot's EVAP system runs a key-off pressure decay test. P1457 indicates the leak is on the canister side rather than tank side. Common cause is the canister vent solenoid sticking open or its hose cracking.

This is a frequent code on 2009-2015 Pilot models.
safetyImpact: No safety impact; emissions failure.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test EVAP
fixSteps.instruction: Introduce smoke at service port, find leak source.

fixSteps.title: Replace vent valve
fixSteps.instruction: Located on canister, behind rear suspension.

faq.a: Minimal; mostly an emissions concern.

title: Ridgeline Random Cylinder Misfire Detected
shortDescription: Random misfire on Ridgeline 3.5L V6 with VCM cylinder deactivation.
fullDescription:
Honda's Variable Cylinder Management deactivates 3 cylinders under cruise. P1399 on the Ridgeline often relates to VCM transitions producing misfires due to ring wear or stuck lifters.

Aftermarket VCM disable devices are commonly used as a workaround.
safetyImpact: Vibration and possible catalyst overheating if persistent.

causes.cause: Worn piston rings on dormant cylinders

fixSteps.title: Read misfire counters
fixSteps.instruction: Identify which cylinders count misfires.

fixSteps.title: Compression test
fixSteps.instruction: Check for low compression on rear bank.

fixSteps.title: Replace plugs/coils
fixSteps.instruction: Update plugs to OE iridium spec.

faq.a: An aftermarket VCM-disable plug is a common preventive measure.

title: Odyssey Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open
shortDescription: IMRC valve stuck in open position on Honda Odyssey 3.5L.
fullDescription:
The Odyssey uses runner control flaps for low-RPM torque. P1077 indicates the runners aren't closing, typically from a failed IMRC actuator or carbon-stuck flaps.

Common on 2011-2017 Odyssey.
safetyImpact: Reduced low-end torque; no immediate safety concern.

fixSteps.title: Inspect actuator movement
fixSteps.instruction: Watch flap arm during key-on test.

fixSteps.title: Clean intake runners
fixSteps.instruction: Spray throttle body cleaner with engine off.

fixSteps.title: Replace IMRC actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Bolts to intake manifold.

faq.a: Usually no, but you'll notice weak takeoff.

title: Pilot VTEC System Malfunction
shortDescription: VTEC oil pressure switch or solenoid failure on Honda Pilot.
fullDescription:
P1259 indicates the VTEC system did not engage when commanded. The Pilot's J35 V6 uses VTEC for high-RPM cam profile changes.

Cause is typically a clogged solenoid screen, low oil pressure, or wiring issue.
safetyImpact: Loss of high-RPM power; engine still drives normally.

fixSteps.title: Check oil level
fixSteps.instruction: Verify oil is at full mark and not contaminated.

fixSteps.title: Replace VTEC solenoid filter
fixSteps.instruction: Small screen in solenoid mount surface.

fixSteps.title: Test pressure switch
fixSteps.instruction: Measure switch resistance per FSM.

faq.a: No, but you'll lose top-end power and FE may drop.

title: Odyssey Electronic Throttle Control System
shortDescription: ETC system fault detected on Honda Odyssey, throttle authority limited.
fullDescription:
The Odyssey ETC monitors throttle position via dual TPS. P1582 sets when the ECM disagrees with the throttle body's reported position. Often caused by carbon on the throttle plate or contaminated TPS.

Vehicle enters reduced-power 'limp' mode.
safetyImpact: Significantly reduced power; merge or hill-climb may be unsafe.

fixSteps.title: Clean throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean with TB cleaner; do not use brake cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Reset throttle adaptation
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool to relearn idle.

fixSteps.title: Replace throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: If cleaning fails, install new unit and relearn.

faq.q: Can I drive in limp mode?

title: Bronco Unable to Bleed Up Fuel Tank
shortDescription: EVAP purge cannot draw vacuum on Bronco fuel tank during self-test.
fullDescription:
P1450 on the Bronco indicates the EVAP system can't develop the required vacuum. Often a stuck-open vent valve, restricted purge line, or fuel cap issue.

Common on 2021+ Bronco 2.3L EcoBoost.
safetyImpact: Slight fuel odor possible, no drivability impact.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuel cap
fixSteps.instruction: Try a new OE cap first.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test EVAP
fixSteps.instruction: Introduce smoke to identify leaks.

fixSteps.title: Replace vent valve
fixSteps.instruction: Located on charcoal canister.

faq.q: Is the Bronco safe to drive?
faq.a: Yes, this is purely an emissions code.

title: Maverick Crankshaft Position System Variation
shortDescription: Crank position sensor variation not learned on Ford Maverick Hybrid.
fullDescription:
The Maverick Hybrid 2.5L Atkinson engine requires a misfire profile correlation learn after CKP sensor or ECM replacement. P1336 means the routine has not completed.

Must be performed with FORScan or factory IDS.
safetyImpact: No drivability concern; misfire detection accuracy reduced until completed.

fixSteps.title: Run CKP variation learn
fixSteps.instruction: Follow FORScan PCM Misfire Profile procedure.

fixSteps.title: Verify completion
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm 'Done' status, clear codes.

title: Mach-E High-Voltage Battery Cell Imbalance
shortDescription: Cell voltage imbalance detected in Mach-E HV battery pack.
fullDescription:
The Mach-E BMS monitors all 376 cells. P1A0F sets when the spread between highest and lowest cell exceeds threshold, indicating a weak module.

Usually fixed under HV battery warranty (8yr/100k mi).
safetyImpact: Reduced range and possibility of HV system shutdown; do not delay service.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coolant level
fixSteps.instruction: Check HV battery coolant reservoir.

fixSteps.instruction: Submit warranty claim; pack opens at dealer.

title: Bronco 7MGE Auto Start-Stop Disable Fault
shortDescription: Auto Start-Stop system disabled and reporting fault on Bronco.
fullDescription:
The Bronco's start-stop monitors battery state-of-charge via an IBS sensor. P1336 (Ford-specific variant) indicates the IBS reports a SOC too low or signal issue.

Not safety-critical but annoying; often fixed by battery replacement.
safetyImpact: No safety impact; loss of fuel-saving feature.

fixSteps.instruction: Load test AGM battery; replace if SOH below 75%.

fixSteps.instruction: Reseat connector at negative battery cable.

fixSteps.title: Replace AGM battery
fixSteps.instruction: Use OE-spec H7 AGM and register via FORScan.

faq.q: Can I use a regular battery?
faq.a: No, AGM is required and must be registered to BMS.

title: Maverick Hybrid Inverter Coolant Temperature High
shortDescription: Inverter coolant temperature exceeded threshold on Maverick Hybrid.
fullDescription:
The Maverick Hybrid uses a dedicated inverter coolant loop. P1471 sets when the inverter coolant exceeds ~85C, often from low coolant or failed pump.

The vehicle may derate to gas-only mode to protect electronics.
safetyImpact: Reduced hybrid capability and overheat risk; pull over if warnings escalate.

fixSteps.instruction: Front reservoir, separate from engine coolant.

fixSteps.title: Bleed coolant loop
fixSteps.instruction: Use vacuum-fill tool per Ford procedure.

fixSteps.title: Replace coolant pump
fixSteps.instruction: Electric pump on inverter housing.

faq.a: Mostly no, but the system may run gas-only and lose hybrid efficiency.

title: Tahoe Ignition 1 Switch Circuit 2
shortDescription: Ignition voltage feed circuit 2 fault on Chevy Tahoe.
fullDescription:
The Tahoe powertrain uses two ignition feeds for redundancy. P1682 sets when feed 2 voltage doesn't match feed 1, often from a corroded fuse holder or faulty ignition switch.

Can cause intermittent stalling on 2015+ Tahoe.
safetyImpact: Risk of stalling; address promptly.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fuses
fixSteps.instruction: Pull and inspect ignition feed fuses for green corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Measure feed voltages
fixSteps.instruction: Both feeds should match within 0.2V.

fixSteps.title: Replace ignition switch
fixSteps.instruction: Located on column.

faq.a: Yes, intermittent stalling is possible until repaired.

title: Silverado Intake Air Flow System Performance
shortDescription: MAF sensor or intake leak on Silverado 5.3L V8.
fullDescription:
P1101 is widespread on GM 5.3L trucks. The ECM sees expected vs actual airflow mismatch, usually from a dirty MAF, dirty throttle body, or PCV-related vacuum leak.

GM has issued multiple TSBs covering this code.
safetyImpact: Possible stalling and reduced fuel economy.

fixSteps.title: Clean MAF
fixSteps.instruction: Use MAF-specific cleaner only.

fixSteps.title: Clean throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: Manual clean with TB cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test intake
fixSteps.instruction: Find unmetered air leaks.

faq.a: Yes, P1101 is one of the most reported codes on GM trucks.

title: Bolt EV High-Voltage Battery Performance
shortDescription: HV battery performance below threshold on Chevrolet Bolt EV.
fullDescription:
Set after the Bolt battery recall remediation, P1AAA can re-trigger if a remaining cell shows abnormal capacity loss. The BECM monitors per-module SOH.

Vehicles affected by the LG cell recall received pack replacements 2021-2023.
safetyImpact: Charging may be limited to 80% or vehicle disabled if severe.

fixSteps.title: Check recall status
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm VIN against N212343940 recall.

fixSteps.title: Update BECM software
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer must apply latest calibrations.

fixSteps.title: Replace battery pack
fixSteps.instruction: Performed under recall warranty.

faq.a: Yes for affected VINs; replacement is at no cost to owner.

title: Suburban MAP/MAF Correlation
shortDescription: MAP and MAF sensor disagreement on Chevy Suburban 6.2L L86.
fullDescription:
The Suburban's ECM cross-checks MAP vs MAF airflow. P1101 (correlation variant) trips when the two disagree by more than threshold, often from AFM lifter collapse causing erratic vacuum.

A known issue on 6.2L Active Fuel Management engines.
safetyImpact: AFM lifter collapse can cause cam wear; address quickly.

title: Bolt EV Ignition Switch Run/Crank Position Circuit
shortDescription: Run/crank ignition signal mismatch on Bolt EV.
fullDescription:
Although the Bolt EV has no crank, the BCM still uses run/start logic. P1682 reports the run signal is missing or contradicts START. Often a failed BCM or PRNDL switch.

Can prevent vehicle from going into READY mode.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may not enter READY; safety-critical for daily use.

fixSteps.instruction: AGM aux battery often weak on Bolt.

fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM AGM only.

fixSteps.title: Inspect start button circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Check wiring from button to BCM.

title: Frontier Engine Over Temperature Condition
shortDescription: Engine coolant temperature exceeded threshold on Nissan Frontier.
fullDescription:
P1217 on the Frontier sets when ECT exceeds about 117C. Often from radiator clogged with debris (off-roading), failed thermostat, or water pump.

The ECM may pull timing to protect the engine.
safetyImpact: Engine damage risk; pull over if temperature gauge reads high.

fixSteps.instruction: Top off only when cold.

fixSteps.instruction: Standard service item.

fixSteps.instruction: Find leaks at hoses or pump.

title: Pathfinder A/F Sensor 1 Bank 1 Lean Shift
shortDescription: Air-fuel sensor reports lean condition on Pathfinder VQ35.
fullDescription:
The Pathfinder's wideband AFR sensor monitors mixture in real time. P1273 sets when the sensor consistently reports lean even with positive fuel trim correction.

Often a vacuum leak or failed AFR sensor.
safetyImpact: Lean operation may damage catalyst over time.

title: Nissan Z Ignition Signal Primary

fullDescription:
The Z's twin-turbo VR30DDTT engine uses individual coil-on-plug ignition. P1320 indicates the ECM lost the primary ignition feedback from one or more coils.

Most often a failed coil pack or harness chafing under the intake.

title: Frontier ICC Steering Switch

fullDescription:
The Frontier intelligent cruise control uses redundant resistor-network switches in the steering wheel. P1564 sets when the resistance is out of range.

Often a worn clock spring or stuck button.

The Tiguan uses retarded cam timing and rich AFR briefly after cold start to heat the catalyst. P11AB sets when the strategy can't reach catalyst temperature in time.
